title: Suspicious authentication failure burst
summary: Triage steps for a burst of failed logins from one source IP against one account.
steps: Confirm whether the source IP is expected for the account owner (VPN, office, travel).
Check whether any successful login followed the failures within the same window.
Compare the account's normal login hours and source geography.
Contact the account owner through a channel other than the one under suspicion.
If a successful login followed the burst, treat the account as potentially compromised and escalate.

title: Password spraying across many accounts
summary: Handling a pattern where one source tries few passwords against many accounts.
steps: Count distinct usernames targeted by the source IP in the window.
Check for a successful login from the same source IP.
Review whether the source IP appears in other alerts or audit records.
Escalate to the identity team; consider forced password reset for affected accounts.

title: Evidence collection and chain of custody
summary: How to assemble and cite evidence for an investigation report.
steps: Cite only event identifiers that exist in the imported data set.
Order the timeline by event timestamp and keep it consistent with the cited evidence.
State explicitly which telemetry sources are missing from the analysis.
Record limitations rather than filling gaps with assumptions.

title: Response boundaries for automated triage
summary: What an automated investigation may and may not do.
steps: Automated triage is read-only: no blocking, disabling, deleting, or scanning.
Every recommendation requires human review before action.
Report conclusions must be traceable to specific event identifiers.
Escalate to a human analyst when evidence is incomplete.
